newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money slips amid high liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money slips amid high liquidity.

text.p: * Volume falls to 10.361 billion from 15.883 billion pesos

Manila overnight money dipped to an average of 10.53125 percent on Tuesday from 10.5625 percent due to a shot of liquidity from the maturity of five billion pesos worth of floating rate treasury notes, traders said.
Rates were locked from 10.5625 to 10.53125 percent in a market with 21 lenders and 19 borrowers.
Traders said this week would see a net inflow of one billion pesos after taking into account investments in T-bills and notes.
Due to the high liquidity in the market, a foreign bank dealer said "all banks are trying to grab assets."
He said the secondary market for T-bills saw active buying in all maturities.

"The view has changed. We're likely to see low interest rates to prevail for some time," he said, adding that the Central Bank has kept its overnight borrowing rate at 10.5 percent for almost two months.
More liquidity is also expected from foreign investors after the Philippines was upgraded one notch by Standard and Poor's Corp, dealers said.

A Reuter poll of seven financial institutions showed them with bid rates of 10.55 to 10.675 percent on the three-month bills; 10.95 to 11.10 percent on six-month bills; and 11.40 to 11.55 percent on one-year bills.
